images.filename: 2026-06-05 refilling the reflecting pool Washington DC 10-50-40.jpg
images.caption: After completing painting the reflecting pool a very, very dark blue, the pool is being refilled.  The project is being done as part of the United States Semiquincentennial.  The pool is between the Lincoln Memorial and the World War II memorial. This is a view looking towards the WWII memorial, several trucks are still in the basin and someone is power-washing part of the bottom. In front of the reflecting pool the West Branch Area School District Band from Morrisdale, Pennsylvania plays a song. National Mall, Washington, DC. June 5, 2026.

images.filename: 2026-06-17 Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool post-restoration Washington DC 18-53-22.jpg
images.caption: The Washington Monument reflecting in the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool after the pool was restored and painted blue.  There is currently an algae bloom being cleaned up and equipment related to that cleanup is visible on the right side of the pool. At this point the algae has been cleared from the water and has settled on the bottom of the pool. In some places it has been vacuumed up but in other places the bottom of the pool is green.  Since the Washington Monument and the sky is being reflected, the color of the water and base of the pool isn't clearly visible. There are also temporary lights lining both sides of the reflecting pool. National Mall, Washington, DC. June 17, 2026.

images.filename: Lincoln memorial seen from washington memorial.jpg
images.caption:
Part of the National Mall with World War II Memorial, reflectihg pool and Lincoln Memorial.
The Lincoln Memorial is a United States Presidential memorial built to honor the 16th President of the United States, Abraham Lincoln. 
The Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool is the largest of Washington, D.C.'s reflecting pools. Located directly east of the Lincoln Memorial, it is a long, rectangular pool visible in many photographs of the Washington Monument. It is lined by walking paths and shade trees on both sides. It reflects both the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial.
The U.S. National World War II Memorial is a National Memorial dedicated to Americans who served in the armed forces and as civilians during World War II. 

The final design consists of 56 pillars, each 5 m tall, arranged in a semicircle around a plaza with two 13 m arches on opposite sides. Two-thirds of the 7.4-acre (30,000 m2) site is landscaping and water. Each pillar is inscribed with the name of one of the 48 U.S. states of 1945, as well as the District of Columbia, the Alaska Territory and Territory of Hawaii, the Commonwealth of the Philippines, Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The northern arch is inscribed with "Atlantic"; the southern one, "Pacific."
